question.:question/worked-solution:

- The set $\mathbb{N}$ contains the positive integers (natural numbers). Therefore, $6.1$ does not belong to $\mathbb{N}$.

- The set $\mathbb{Q}_0^{+}$ contains the nonnegative rational numbers. Therefore, $6.1$ belongs to $\mathbb{Q}_0^{+}$.

- The set $\mathbb{N}_0$ contains the nonnegative integers. Therefore, $6.1$ does not belong to $\mathbb{N}_0$.

- The set $\mathbb{R}_0^{+}$ contains the nonnegative real numbers. Therefore, $6.1$ belongs to $\mathbb{R}_0^{+}$.

Therefore, select $\mathbb{Q}_0^{+}$, $\mathbb{R}_0^{+}$ only.

- The set $\mathbb{R}_0^{-}$ contains the nonpositive real numbers. Therefore, $-\sqrt{82}$ belongs to $\mathbb{R}_0^{-}$.

- The set $\mathbb{Z}^{-}$ contains the negative integers. Therefore, $-\sqrt{82}$ does not belong to $\mathbb{Z}^{-}$.

- The set $\mathbb{Z}_0^{+}$ contains the nonnegative integers. Therefore, $-\sqrt{82}$ does not belong to $\mathbb{Z}_0^{+}$.

- The set $\mathbb{C}$ contains all complex numbers. Therefore, $-\sqrt{82}$ belongs to $\mathbb{C}$.

Therefore, select "I and IV only".
